title: Inheritance and Confession
premise: When a fresh corpse is discovered wearing clothes stolen from Sable Delacroix's own closet, the true-crime podcaster realizes someone has been studying them as closely as they've studied Ashford Hollow's coldest case: the 1994 disappearance of heiress Marguerite Voss. As Sable re-interviews witnesses whose alibis were stitched together thirty years ago, they uncover a conspiracy among the town's founding families to bury not one death but two—and to make Sable the perfect scapegoat for both. The killer is Marguerite's presumed-dead sister, who has been living in plain sight as the town's beloved archivist, and the final confession comes only after Sable risks becoming the next body in the archive.
about_author: Xanthe Iversen is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering unsolved cases across the Rust Belt before turning to fiction. They write from a farmhouse full of filing cabinets, which they insist are 'organized, not obsessive.'

chapters.title: The Alphabet of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In their basement archive, Sable records the hundredth episode about the Marguerite Voss disappearance, revealing a small inconsistency in the original police timeline. The beat is quiet competence masking loneliness; Sable has made the dead case their only real relationship.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Called to the old Voss boathouse by a tip, Sable finds a fresh corpse dressed in clothes from their own closet—clothes they can prove were stolen days earlier. Detective Imogen Reyes arrives and treats Sable as suspect first, source second. The beat: the hunter realizes they are also prey.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Polite Silence
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable canvasses the founding families—the Hales, the Merricks, the Voss estate lawyer—and notes how smoothly each deflects, their alibis word-for-word identical to 1994 statements. The beat is dread: the town rehearsed this story long before Sable was born.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Kindness
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Town archivist Edith Voss, Marguerite's 'cousin,' offers Sable access to sealed family papers and warm, disarming hospitality. Sable, starved for belonging, is tempted to trust her. The beat: comfort that reads, in hindsight, as reconnaissance.

chapters.title: What the Tape Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Imogen Reyes's POV. Reyes reviews the 911 call from 1994 and finds a ninety-second gap before dispatch answered—someone cut the tape. She begins quietly pulling Sable's phone records. The beat: institutional suspicion tightening around the protagonist.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ground-penetrating radar, borrowed from a listener, reveals a second body beneath the Voss orchard—Marguerite herself, never missing at all, dead since 1994. The cold case becomes a murder case with a thirty-year head start. Beat: vertigo.

chapters.title: Alibi, Stitched and Restitched
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable maps the 1994 alibis and finds they only work if the witnesses lied in concert—a pact. One witness, the drunk former groundskeeper, almost talks, then recants after a visit from someone Sable can't identify. Beat: the walls have ears.

chapters.title: Closet Inventory
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Reyes traces the stolen clothes to a break-in that happened while Sable was on air, live—an alibi someone clearly wanted to build for them. She begins to wonder who benefits from framing Sable. Beat: reluctant alliance forming.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The Voss will, read aloud thirty years ago, left everything to Marguerite 'or, failing her, her sister'—a sister whose death certificate Sable can't find. Edith's claim to be a cousin begins to unravel. Beat: the inheritance itself is the motive.

chapters.title: Night at the Merrick House
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable breaks into the Merrick mansion during a fundraiser and finds the 1994 alibi letters, all in the same hand. They photograph them and are nearly caught by patriarch Aldous Merrick. Beat: trespass, adrenaline, first hard proof of conspiracy.

chapters.title: Threats, Filed and Alphabetized
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Anonymous notes start arriving in Sable's own archival handwriting style—someone mimicking them, building a paper trail of 'obsession.' The frame tightens: notes, stolen clothes, proximity to both bodies. Beat: Sable's identity as investigator is being overwritten as killer.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Confession
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The groundskeeper dies of an 'accident' hours before Reyes can interview him, but leaves her a voicemail: 'She was never gone. She was never gone.' Reyes plays it for Sable; they pool what they know. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Last Summer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Through recovered letters, Sable reconstructs 1994: Marguerite planned to expose the families' land-fraud scheme and leave town, disinheriting everyone. Someone silenced her before the town meeting. Beat: the victim becomes the story's true hero.

chapters.title: A Name on the Death Certificate
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A records clerk in another county confirms it: Marguerite's sister, Colette Voss, died at nine years old—or someone buried a child's identity. Edith's birthday matches Colette's exactly. Beat: the kindly archivist becomes the prime suspect.

chapters.title: The Trap We Set Ourselves
chapters.summary: Sable and Reyes's POV, alternating. They leak a false detail—that the orchard bones are being exhumed—to force the killer's hand. Instead, the killer burns the boathouse and plants Sable's podcast equipment in the ashes. Beat: the trap springs the wrong way.

chapters.title: Suspended
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Reyes is suspended for collaborating with a suspect; the town council—descendants of the 1994 signatories—applies pressure from above. Sable is formally charged. Beat: the institutions built to protect the town protect only its liars.

chapters.title: What Sable Kept Hidden
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cornered, Sable admits to Reyes the thing they've buried: five years ago they quietly destroyed a tape that implicated Edith in small forgeries, because Edith was the only person who'd ever made them feel they belonged. Beat: shame, and the theme of belonging turned inward.

chapters.title: The Archive After Hours
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable confronts Edith in the town archive at night. Edith, calm and almost tender, confesses she is Colette—left for dead by the family, returned under a dead child's name, and killing to reclaim what the inheritance stole. The new victim was her accomplice who threatened to talk. Beat: the confession, delivered like a gift.

chapters.title: Belonging, Weaponized
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Edith reveals the frame was designed to make Sable's archive the killer's archive—every episode a confession by proxy. She offers Sable a choice: join her, inherit the story, finally belong. Beat: temptation at knife's edge.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Sable and Reyes's POV. Sable keeps Edith talking while Reyes, tipped off despite suspension, records from the stacks. Edith realizes, and the archive becomes a maze of shelves and fire. Beat: the climax—truth as a weapon, and the cost of wielding it.

chapters.title: Ash and Evidence
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Edith is arrested as the archive burns; the alibi letters, the will, and Marguerite's letters survive because Sable digitized everything years ago. The founding families' 1994 pact is exposed; arrests ripple outward. Beat: vindication, but the town Sable documented is gone.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred One
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable airs the final episode: Marguerite's story, told as hers, not the town's. They pack the archive into boxes—not alphabetized—and consider leaving Ashford Hollow, belonging now carried rather than sought. Beat: quiet, earned release.
